prs.body:
Missions stream, handoff §6 item 2: **Plain Words**. Stacked on the activity-ui PR; review only the Plain Words commits.

## What changes
- **Boards.** Twenty sandwich boards stand on the Columbus Ave sidewalks between the real Broadway and Bay St junctions. They're generated from the road graph: outside the Chinatown analysis neighbourhood, at least 15 m from Grant Ave and Stockton St, on open ground (`content/activity-rules.json` `plainWords.boards`). The checkpoints move onto the real junctions; the Columbus/Bay point was 170 m off.
- **Washing, measured.** Each tick the player's own water particles are swept through each board (the player adapter adds `waterTraces` to the gameplay context). Two seconds of stream turns a board back to plain words and raises `board.washed`. Claimed `board.washed` facts never count.
- **Sign-spinners.** Starting the activity asks the agents runtime for four bad sign-spinner robots, through the existing `mission.scene-request` path, beside the southern boards. Standing spinners rebrand washed boards every 8 s within 50 m. Every four rebrands the hype word climbs the ladder. At "made by humans" a rebrand counts as plain words, as the design says ("the hype ate itself"). A rusted spinner stops. A run's spinners retire when it ends.
- **Completion, as `docs/design.md` states it:** twenty washes and every spinner rusted, inside five minutes. The three checkpoints mark the corridor and its start; no route is required.
- **HUD.** Progress, the hype word, and minimap blips for rebranded boards and standing spinners.

- Unit tests (`tests/sim/player/plain-words.test.ts`): washing, missed and foreign water, claimed facts, rebrands and the ladder, rusted spinners, payout and timeout.

prs.title: Missions: Launch Day real-SF browser playthrough, two-player session, curbside save spawn
prs.body:
Missions stream, handoff §6 item 1: Launch Day and Demo'd Correctly played through real controls in the real SF world.

## What changes
- **Loaded saves no longer strand the car.** The restore put the car on the safehouse pin. The FiDi desk pin is 41 m from any lane, in a 2 m passage, so the car could not drive out. `src/save/restore-spawn.ts` now places it on the nearest drivable lane, facing along it. `tests/ui/restore-spawn.test.ts` checks every safehouse on the real map.
- **Closed-loop drivers** for Launch Day and Demo'd Correctly (`tests/helpers/drivers/wave3-campaign.ts`). They plan from observed state and step only the production simulation.
  - When driving meets a jam, the driver brakes for traffic and creeps behind people.
  - It overtakes only through a swept corridor, and leaves the carriageway only where no one stands nearby.
  - Failing that, it rewinds and tries another plan; traffic is deterministic, so only the plan that arrives stays in the recorded inputs.
  - Where the mission allows any travel mode, it walks the street route.
- **Long real-SF playthroughs** run in their own config, `tests/e2e/campaign-long.config.ts` (`*.long.ts`). They take an hour or more under SwiftShader, beyond the default suite's CI budget.
  - `campaign-launch-day.long.ts`:
    - A post-Spill save goes in through the save panel's Import and Load.
    - Launch Day is played with real controls and the page's own dialogs: drive or walk to Washington Square, Watch, Bot Check, the false positive and its Continue, compare, melt, then the pivot form.
    - It saves mid-mission and after completion, then reloads both ways.
    - A second attempt fails on its clock and is retried with fresh actors.
    - Each page session's Node replay must match the page's hash. Rewards are paid once, with zero protected contacts.
  - `campaign-two-players.long.ts`:
    - p2 joins through `player.join` and plays Hot Desk, with its commands arriving as events, while p1 plays Launch Day.
    - It checks actor bindings, each player's own guidance (`uiProjection`) and once-only rewards, including after a reload on each client.
- **Test plumbing:** closing a dialog resumes the game clock, so the helpers hold it again after closing.

## Evidence
- In the browser on `?world=sf` (integrate/wave2 `ff7db5b`, before the v10 merge), the first Launch Day session completed:
  - 32,136 input frames and 5 recorded commands.
  - Exact Node replay, hash `b439bf4c`.
  - Scanner tier 2, `launch-day:complete` paid once, courier dry, zero contacts.
  - The reload-after-completion checks passed.
  - That run then reached my old one-hour test limit in the retry phase. The new file allows four hours.
- Node, real SF: Launch Day completes from the restored save through real inputs only. The two-player Hot Desk leg (p2) completes in 14,625 frames with p1 untouched and zero contacts.

## Not done / blocked (honest status)
- **Demo'd Correctly cannot yet be finished in the browser.** It needs the car at Pier 70, and every driving plan out of the FiDi desk stalls in ambient-traffic gridlock. The deadlock is diagnosed in `docs/parallel/status/missions-stream.md` and fixed in #38. With #38 merged locally, the walkers no longer freeze, but robotaxi queues still stall these routes. I'm investigating with the City life stream.
- The long specs have not yet been re-run after merging integrate/wave2 (`86dfb90`, SIM_VERSION 10); that re-run is in progress.
- CI: `.github` is the Harness's. The long config needs its own CI job; I've asked the coordinator.

None. No `SIM_VERSION` change.

prs.title: World detail: lawns, fences and piers (needs OSM/ODbL sign-off)
prs.body:
**Stacked on #53 (street signs), #52 and #41.** The new work is `pipeline/lib/landcover.ts`, `pipeline/lib/osm-pbf.ts` and `src/render/street-landcover.ts`.

## ⚠️ Owner decision needed: OpenStreetMap (ODbL)

This is the first OpenStreetMap data in the repo. Fort Mason's Great Meadow, the Presidio and Crissy Field (land the city doesn't map) and most fences and piers exist only in OSM. Two requirements follow from the ODbL:
- The OSM-derived data is kept in its own file, `public/tiles/sf/street-osm.json`, which is a **derivative database under the ODbL** (its `license` field says so). DataSF data stays in `street-landcover.json`.
- The game must show "© OpenStreetMap contributors" where it shows credits. The line is in `street-detail.json` `attribution`; **the credits UI (UI-Audio) needs to display it.**

`docs/data-sources.md` said "No OpenStreetMap data is used"; it now says the world build uses none and the street-detail land cover does. If you'd rather not ship OSM, drop `street-osm.json` and the `osm` layer: the DataSF parts still work on their own.

The extract is the pinned one your local session pushed on `data/osm-sf` (`ec64af5`, SHA-256 `90f1a33c…f3be4`, OSM timestamp 2026-10-22). The producer reads it from `data/osm/` and checks the hash. **This PR does not add the 18.6 MB .pbf.** Merging `data/osm-sf` is needed only to rebuild, not to run the game.

## What

- **Grass**:
  - Rec and Park lawns: *Functional Areas* `38b7-6db3` Lawn, Non-landscaped Greenspace and Natural Area (Marina Green, the Palace of Fine Arts, every city park).
  - OSM grass (`landuse=grass/meadow`, `landcover=grass`, `natural=grassland`, grass pitches; ways and multipolygons with holes).
  - Clipped to 100 m cells and drawn as a terrain-following sheet just above the ground, below the road ribbons.
- **Fences, walls, hedges**: Rec and Park *Linear Assets* `rny7-88gk` Fence/Gate, plus OSM `barrier=fence/wall/retaining_wall/hedge/guard_rail`. Fences render as posts with a chain-link panel; walls and hedges as blocks.
- **Piers**: OSM `man_made=pier` (the Marina's yacht-harbour docks, Fort Mason, the Embarcadero), as decks above the sea.
- `pipeline/lib/osm-pbf.ts` is a small dependency-free PBF reader (zlib blobs, dense nodes, ways, relations).

## Files outside the stream's own

`src/render/scene.ts` (passes the sea height), `src/debug.ts`, `tests/schemas/schemas.test.ts`.

## Tests

`tests/pipeline/landcover.test.ts` covers:
- cell clipping keeps area and holes;
- grass drapes on the ground and leaves holes bare;
- OSM tag classes;
- joining multipolygons from member ways;
- on the committed data: the Great Meadow and Marina Green lawns are grassed, and Fort Mason has fences and the Marina has piers.

## Evidence

`docs/shots/world-detail/landcover-*.png` (Fort Mason meadow before/after and from above, Marina Green, Bay St, fences).

prs.title: World (a): structural world import as SIM_VERSION 14, source snapshot and reproducibility
prs.body:
World stream PR (a) of a stack: (a) source cache and reproducibility → (b) generator/collision/sweep fixes → (c) structural physics v9, migration and agent surfaces → (d) renderer wiring.

**Draft. Do not merge yet.** This PR imports the held structural world, and the strict world gate is red on it. Most of that is pre-existing on `qa/world-integration`; PR (b) clears it. It becomes ready only when CI is green.

## What this does

- **Imports the structural SF world** by merging `qa/world-integration` (`4556f8a`) onto `integrate/wave2` as a merge commit, so the original authorship is kept. That branch brings structural surfaces (decks, tunnel bores, stair barriers, inland water), the regenerated SF tiles, the band-aware sweep, the strict world gates and the Lake Merced propulsion fix (780 m → 0 m). Conflicts were resolved by keeping wave2's registry, parking/street-cleaning/transit/sidewalk layers, quarantine, lifecycle, combat and per-attempt mission ids. Only comments and version stamps were combined.
- **Reproducibility.** The original raw cache is gone: it is in no git ref, and the pipeline never recorded input hashes. DataSF answers again, so the pinned datasets were refetched; DataSF has no as-of queries, so this is today's data. An offline `--check` against that cache reproduced **1,192 of 1,203 files byte-for-byte**: the collider pack, every collider, roads, boundary, gameplay and every far cell. The 11 differences all come from the daily business registry (`g8m3-pdis`): storefront anchors went 10,478 → 10,481, plus `report.json` counters and nine tile GLBs that draw shopfronts.
- **Explicit new snapshot `2026-10-23T21:20Z`**, not a silent refresh:
  - `pipeline/source-snapshot.json` pins the SHA-256 and size of all 181 raw responses (389.7 MB).
  - `pipeline/tools/source-snapshot.ts` writes it and verifies a cache against it.
  - `docs/data-sources.md` "Snapshots" records the date, the hashes and the diff summary.
  - The tiles were regenerated by the pipeline. No GLB or pack was hand-edited.
- Merge fallout fixed: duplicate `World` fields, a duplicate import, the sf-world layer list (gameplay + storefronts), version tests, and the docs/testing.md index for the three new e2e specs.

## Contract changes

- `SIM_VERSION` → **14** (additive; integrate now ships v10 weather, v11 player feel, v12 robotaxi rides and v13 city life/unlimited water, so the structural world takes current + 1). The structural physics are stamped 9 in the same commit that imports them, so they never reach a branch targeting `integrate/wave2` under a gameplay-only stamp. `upgradeState` chains … → v12 → v13 → v14, each step written previous → this, with no saved field rewritten; v9 is never written. Every shipped fixture (v7, v8, v10, v11, v12, v13) is unchanged. New pins:
  - `tests/golden/composed-v14.json`: coverage identical to v13 in all five scenarios; only hashes moved, because the version is hashed.
  - `tests/golden/wave2-v14.json`.

  PR (c) adds surface-aware load/join recovery and real-save 8→9 tests.

## Known red (pre-existing on `qa/world-integration`; same tests run on a pristine checkout)

- The strict `world-pr` gate: 53 passed / 78 failed / 7 skipped. Of 116 metrics, 67 are better, 37 the same and 12 worse. PR (b) fixes the worse ones and tightens the reviewed improvements.
- `tests/sim/boundary.test.ts`, southern edge: the 2.1978 m is the probe's own start pose straddling a shoreline wall notch. From every clear start the car stops with 0.000 m overshoot. PR (b) fixes the probe and keeps the 0.02 m assertion.
- `tests/sim/pack.test.ts`: the test compares raw `ground` objects, but the pack carries lakes as a `lake` array while the JSON carries `cover` digits, by design. Fixed in PR (b) with a stronger equivalence check.
- `tests/golden/world-baseline.test.ts`, ground-tint wiring: resolved by the renderer's `bakedGround` guard in PR (d).
- `tests/sim/sf-agents.test.ts`, one agent entering a building: PR (c), banded motion and agent surfaces.
- **Two browser regressions found by CI** (run 40044165274, attempt 2), not yet root-caused, tracked for this stack:
  - `car-pose.spec.ts`: `G.far.cellsDrawnFromTwinPeaks` is 9 far cells against a baseline of 13 (W-20 is marked fixed, so this is a hard regression).
  - `sf-world.spec.ts`, "the city limit has no crack": 6 far quads stitched at the southern edge, where more than 50 are required.

  Both concern the far layer meeting the structural tiles in the current renderer. Whether the cause is the far-layer output or the renderer's seam logic (the structural renderer, PR (d), handles baked seams) is still open. Neither is waived.

## Outside the World area

- `tests/golden/*`, `tests/helpers*`, `docs/testing.md` (Harness): version pins, golden fixtures and the e2e doc index.
- `content/storefronts.json` and the storefront/house/landmark content schemas are deliberately left out. They land with their content in PR (d).

## Validation

- `pnpm typecheck`: passed.
- Unit project: 3,445 passed / 16 failed before the fallout fixes; the remaining reds are the list above. Content/schema suites: 1,822 passed.
- `node pipeline/build-world.ts --world sf --offline --check` (with the snapshot cache): see the comment below once CI runs.

prs.title: Sim-Player: bank streak rewards and validate wave-4 mission progression
prs.body:
## Summary

Streaks now bank an equipped reward when its threshold is crossed and spend that reward when called. Score is retained, old profiles are adopted once, and re-equipping cannot farm another reward. Canonical and legacy loadout IDs use the same authored rank gates. Wide-nozzle purchases, owned nozzle switching and saved Microclimate selection preserve those gates.

Parking, bell-duel and cable-car mechanics now feed the registered player pipeline through validated world bindings and accepted poses. Measured story objectives and faction routes reject named-fact shortcuts, late handoffs and remote handoffs. The canonical progression Doom Clock handles absolute-day catch-up, same-tick AGI calls and once-only match settlement without a second clock or duplicate faction payouts.

## Roadmap deliverables

- [x] Wave-4 progression gates, banked streak rewards and enabled-perk projection.
- [x] Mission-mechanics adapter with physical acceptance and snapshot replay coverage.
- [x] Reconcile the published wave-4 story, faction and match-isolation work.
- [x] Canonical Doom Clock, Conference Week state and boundary-aware settlements.
- [ ] Production world/provider and visual/mode consumers; remaining wave-4 activities and wave-5–8 work.

## Acceptance tests

- Passed: typecheck and all **164 player/purity tests**, including ownership/rank aliases, snapshot restore, forged completion rejection and producer-cursor poisoning.
- Full unit run: **2,768 passed, four failed, one skipped** with loopback test servers enabled. Remaining failures are inherited content lint (`R-Evolution binder delivery`), missing packaged gameplay layer, the old empty-extension assertion and a pre-player-system replay hash pin.
- Independent adversarial reviews found no remaining blocker after fixing named-fact shortcuts, endpoint/deadline checks and producer-cursor poisoning.
- Passed on the final equipment merge: **all 16 browser determinism checks** (Chromium 8, Firefox 4, WebKit 4), including SF running-game/render isolation and multiplayer replay.

## Contract changes

No new shared contract, content or schema edits in this continuation's diff against `lane/sim-player/wave4`. Optional fields live in lane-owned extension state; the existing canonical `progression.doom` remains authoritative. The published dependency's shared interface/content commits are preserved.

## Requests for other lanes

Core should supply absolute `gameDay`/`gameWeek`, unique actor/objective bindings, accepted mechanics poses and recovered-vehicle ownership through the observed provider. Core, Agents, Render and Modes must consume the clock, Conference Week and perk outputs. The equipment bridge now exposes wide nozzles and Microclimate; the integrating lane must compose their combat runtime. Subscription billing and the before-first-attack producer remain outstanding. Detailed handoff: `docs/parallel/status/sim-player.md`.

## For the owner to judge

This PR targets `lane/sim-player/wave4` and preserves that branch; it does not merge into a release or integration branch. It is an incremental Lane 5 handoff, not a declaration that the complete game or waves 2–8 are finished.

prs.title: Ferry Building showcase: high graphics tier, PBR streets, plaza, F-line and palms (WIP)
prs.body:
Work in progress on the owner's Ferry Building showcase: the 800 m around the clock tower, rendered like a current-gen game. Based on `qa/housekit`, which already includes the qa/pipeline, qa/render, qa/assets and qa/content lanes. **Do not merge ahead of the world QA gate.**

## What's in it so far
- **Graphics tiers** (`src/render/gfx.ts`). `?gfx=high|default|auto` sets the tier, and auto is the default.
  - Auto picks the high tier on a hardware WebGL2 GPU. It picks default on a software rasteriser (every CI and e2e run) or a phone, so the default tier the budget tests measure is unchanged.
  - An auto-chosen high tier that stays under 30 fps for 5 s drops post-processing, then shadows. An explicit `?gfx=high` never steps down.
  - `?gfxoff=post,shadows,detail,showcase,ao,bloom` turns features off for A/B shots.
- **Post-processing** (`post.ts`): N8AO ambient occlusion, bloom, and tone mapping applied once in the output pass. Three's GTAOPass drew the frame black under this scene's 0.5 m–20 km depth range, so it is not used.
- **Shadows:** 4096 px sun shadows with a softer PCF kernel in the high tier.
- **Generated PBR detail** (`detail.ts`): the generated texture sets (`assets/textures/generate.py`, WebP, 6 MB, no photographs) are mapped in world space on roads, sidewalks and ground. Grass goes on lawns, and pavers wherever the showcase's mask says.
- **Showcase street layer** (`showcase.ts`):
  - crosswalks (continental on busy streets) and stop bars with worn paint
  - pavers on Harry Bridges Plaza, the Embarcadero median and the waterfront promenade
  - the F-line trackbed and two tracks down the median
  - 58 Canary Island date palms
- Tiles with bores under them now hand their ground material to the scene, so it gets the same detail.
- **Static build:** packs `models/textures/` (WebP and `textures.json`).
- **Privacy test:** every image under `public/models/textures/` must come from the generator.
- **New pinned dependencies:** `n8ao` 2.0.1 and `postprocessing` 6.39.5 (n8ao imports it).

## Still to do
- Kerbs, then the hero Ferry Building model (arcade depth, tower detail, roof trusses), and stone, stucco and glass PBR on the buildings within the radius.
- Reflective Bay water, a lighting pass for day, golden hour and night, high-definition avatars, and denser props.
- Tests for the tier choice, the governor, the showcase geometry (nothing on a carriageway) and the build packing.
- Budgets measured on both tiers, then the full suite and the world gate.
- Before-and-after screenshots for the owner. Whether it looks photoreal is the owner's call.

prs.title: Wave 1 integrated with early wave 2: the whole city, traffic and robots, the player's look, and a hostable build
prs.body:
## What this is

The six wave-1 tracks (pipeline, render, sim, content, assets, harness), merged into one game, plus the whole-city world and the runtime that plays it. The early wave-2 content, art and player look are merged on top. Each track was built, then reviewed independently and fixed, before it merged.

## What is in it

- **The whole city.** 583 tiles of 500 m and 175,595 buildings from SF open data: DataSF footprints with LiDAR heights, centerlines, the assessor roll, and USGS 3DEP terrain. Tiles are meshopt-compressed and kept in plain git. The wave-1 tower rule (a tower only where the LiDAR supports one) is reconciled with wave 2's citywide pipeline, and tiles regenerate deterministically from the download cache.
- **Traffic and robots in the game.** The game builds its sim world with the road graph, so robotaxis, Footmen (errand robots), Trundles and people run on it. They are instanced in three distance tiers, interpolated between ticks, and lit at night.
- **The city runtime.**
  - The sim boots from the binary collider pack.
  - The land edge and shore are walled.
  - Traffic runs near players only.
  - The far skyline is drawn to 20 km, the sea sits at sea level, and the parks are green.
- **Wave-2 content (early).**
  - The YC references are renamed to Ramen.
  - 14 invented names are searched and signed off, and Porter is renamed Footman, Clout Humbled.
  - 66 robot tells, 400 barks, 60 Ambient Director cards, and the Hot Desk and Spill missions.
  - A content lint, and a crisis check for typed text.
- **Wave-2 art (early).**
  - One humanoid body for the crowd, baked to vertex-animation textures.
  - The Footman, Trundle and Meander robotaxi remodelled to the design's robot table.
  - The Moat Labs van, props and synthesised sounds.
- **The player's look.** `founder-default` is a stylised likeness of the owner, made at the owner's request from their own photos. The photos are never in the repo, and a test enforces that. It is recorded as the one consented exception to "never real private people".
- **A hostable static build.** It is built from tile packs and boots from any sub-path.
- **Tests and CI.**
  - Cross-engine determinism in Node, Chromium, Firefox and WebKit.
  - Browser tests that hold up under load, and memory-safe test settings.
  - CI runs on every pull request and on pushes to main, and the screenshot step has its own time limit.

## Not ready to merge

This stays a draft until the **world-continuity QA gate** passes. A whole-city audit of buildings, terrain, hills, streets and play continuity found 52 blocker, high and medium defects at 54ee728. Examples:
- streets walled by building footprints;
- the Broadway Tunnel draped over Russian Hill;
- freeways drawn on the ground;
- creek bridges and piers with no decks;
- dry lakes;
- render ground that disagrees with the sim's ground.

A fix round is running on the `qa/*` branches and will merge here, followed by re-audits until nothing new turns up.

## Testing

- On b3d54b6: typecheck; Vitest, 68 files, 2,464 passed and 1 skipped; Playwright, 39 passed. Run with `--maxWorkers=2` and `--workers=1` under the machine's memory limit.
